subject.title: refactor(net): extract guarded one-hop dispatch boundary

question: Should `src/infra/net` own and version `network-guard/v1` as the internal contract that carries SSRF decisions across future connection-owner boundaries?
rationale: The patch creates a durable representation of route, DNS, TLS, and address-policy conclusions for future consumers; code review cannot safely choose its owner, compatibility expectations, or whether a second consumer exists without maintainer intent.

options.title: Keep the contract local for now
options.body: Retain only a local fetch-guard extraction and defer the versioned profile until an approved second connection owner requires it.

options.title: Approve infra/net ownership
options.body: Confirm that `src/infra/net` owns the versioned internal profile, define its intended consumer boundary, and require refreshed proof after rebasing.

recommendation.title: Keep the contract local for now
recommendation.body: Retain only a local fetch-guard extraction and defer the versioned profile until an approved second connection owner requires it.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor is the concrete adjacent owner signal in the discussion because the open managed-egress work owns nearby proxy and transport policy.
